output.brief:
The October night-premium shortfalls were caused by a pay-rule change, not by Fenmarch's data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule NSP-02. It was logged as a label correction with no effect on pay. The template also moved the premium start time from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's audit trail records this, and it was the only rule edit in the period. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 staff who start at 22:00 were paid correctly. Re-running October in the test tenant with the 20:00 start gave correct pay for all 158. The flagged-record theory fails. Those records were paid correctly in the parallel run. The MD-1023 extract Ardentra cites doesn't appear in the load logs. Flagged staff were underpaid at no higher a rate than unflagged staff. Bank transfers matched the payroll file, and platform release 7.4 made no rule changes.

I'm confident in this. Don't suspend the HR team, re-cleanse the data, or accept the clause 14.3 cost. Don't roll back release 7.4, because the November tax table needs it. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start, verify it in the test tenant before 24 Nov, and make off-cycle payments to everyone underpaid. The link between the shortfalls and the fall in night overtime cover is unproven, because the rota trial started at the same time. Pausing the trial now isn't justified. Treat it as a separate question.
